🇲🇽📈 <u>EDOMEX: 1.9 MILLION PEOPLE OUT OF POVERTY</u>

Mexico's most populous state, ruled by the PRI for nearly a century until 2023, now has the numbers: per INEGI's latest measurement, poverty in the State of Mexico fell from 7.4 million people in 2022 to 5.5 million in 2024 — from 42.9% to 31.2%. Delfina Gómez's government has put 55 billion pesos into programs for the elderly, people with disabilities and youth.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MORENA CLOSES RANKS AGAINST FOREIGN-BACKED PRESSURE</u>

Morena leader Ariadna Montiel called for unity ahead of 2027 as the right escalates its campaign against progressive governments across Latin America: "The unity is not around a person, it is around a project… in this moment of harassment of progressive, humanist movements like Morena, we must put the project before the people."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S DEBT: THIRD-LOWEST IN THE OECD</u>

Sheinbaum shut down the "debt explosion" narrative: Mexico ranks third among OECD countries with the lowest public debt relative to GDP — far below the US and Japan. And by law, borrowing goes to infrastructure, not current spending. What matters, she said, is "the capacity to pay maturities," and that "is totally guaranteed."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>FRANCE SENDS A TRADE MISSION TO MEXICO</u>

French Foreign Trade Minister Nicolas Forissier lands in Mexico on September 28-29 with a business delegation — infrastructure, pharma, fintech, telecoms and agritech firms looking for Mexican partners and projects. While Washington threatens tariffs, Europe is lining up to invest. Diversification isn't a slogan; it's arriving on a plane.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SALINAS PLIEGO'S "EMPIRE" GOES INTO BANKRUPTCY CASCADE</u>

The billionaire who spent years dodging the SAT and posing as Mexico's anti-4T savior is now watching his holdings fall into concurso mercantil one after another. TV Azteca was declared in commercial bankruptcy in July, five of its subsidiaries followed, and up to 600 creditors are lining up — its own filing lists 1,970 debts worth 23.3 billion pesos. La Jornada's México SA: "hundreds of creditors are coming for him."

‍FREIGHTWAVES: Borderlands Mexico: Customs proposal raises concerns over border delays, cargo seizures September 27, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Sheinbaum's Customs Law amendment would lower the undervaluation threshold from 50% to 20% and allow precautionary seizures of under-invoiced imports. FreightWaves leads with the "concerns." 🔍 The piece does state the goal of protecting domestic manufacturers. Still, automotive, warehousing and customs-broker warnings outnumber the government's explanation. Under-invoiced Asian imports are the same issue Washington is pressing Mexico on in the USMCA review. • "Undervaluation erodes Mexico's import-tax base" • "could disrupt just-in-time manufacturing"

‍BILLBOARD: Mexico President Announces BTS' 2027 Return After Meeting With South Korea Leader September 24, 2026 | 🟡 📰 South Korea's president made the first Korean state visit to Mexico in 16 years. It produced 17 agreements covering AI, aerospace, defense and crude supply, plus a revised investment treaty after seven years of talks. 🔍 In US media it mostly showed up as a K-pop story: BTS in 2027, and why Stray Kids didn't appear on the balcony. Billboard gives the trade talks half a sentence. Mexico is diversifying partners in the middle of a USMCA review, and that part barely made it into US coverage. • "topics such as trade, technology and the K-pop phenomenon were discussed" • "a center in Mexico dedicated to K-pop culture"
banner: Korea state visit: 17 deals, US sees K-pop

text: ‍AFP/YAHOO: Thousands protest ahead of Mexican president's report on missing students September 27, 2026 | 🟡 📰 AFP gives the Ayotzinapa parents the floor on the 12th anniversary, before Monday's report on the new lines of investigation. 🔍 It says independent experts "rejected the government's conclusion" without naming the government. The incinerated-in-a-river "historical truth" came from Peña Nieto's attorney general in 2015. The current government reopened the case, and an ex-governor was arrested in August. • "Because they were taken alive, we want them back alive" • "Twelve years of suffering, of lies." — Estanislao Mendoza, father of one of the 43 • "the unsolved case remains a stain on Mexico's reputation"

‍BREITBART: Mexican President Blames Raging Cartel Violence on U.S. Meddling September 23, 2026 | 🔴 📰 Breitbart says Sheinbaum is "unable to control" cartel violence. Four paragraphs later, it explains exactly what she said: the Sinaloa war began when Los Chapitos kidnapped El Mayo Zambada and handed him to US authorities in Texas. 🇲🇽 Mexico was not told about that handover. The piece gives no homicide figures, even though national homicides are down about 51%. • "the raging cartel violence that she is unable to control" • "has continued to rely on nationalistic rhetoric" • "the kidnapping of kingpin Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada at the hands of his allies"

‍TPR: The U.S. and Mexico aren't breaking up over cartels. They're arguing over who's to blame. September 27, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Texas Public Radio covered Trump's "epicenter" UN speech and did something rare: it quoted Mexican analysts and spelled out Mexico's case. That case is US drug consumption, US firearms and illicit financial flows. 🔍 TPR counted more than two dozen appearances since January 2025 in which Sheinbaum invoked sovereignty. It also points out that Mexico's Senate authorized 139 US 101st Airborne troops for joint training that her government requested. The piece doesn't mention the 51% drop in homicides that Mexico keeps citing. • "Mexico must reclaim control of its soil from the enemies of humanity." — Trump • Washington frames cartels as "threats entering the United States from abroad"
banner: US-Mexico cartel feud: blame, not breakup
